name: AgensGraph
tagline: PostgreSQL fork with a built-in property graph model, mixing SQL, openCypher and ISO GQL.
description: AgensGraph is a PostgreSQL fork (not an extension) from SKAI Worldwide, formerly Bitnine, that builds the property-graph model into the database: a graph is a schema, labels are tables, and vertices and edges are rows. You can mix SQL, openCypher and ISO GQL clauses in a single statement, and graph data shares transactions, roles, row-level security, replication and extensions such as pgvector with ordinary tables. The 2.18 line is rebased on PostgreSQL 18.6 and adds more GQL clauses and planner improvements. It suits Postgres shops that want deeper graph integration than the AGE extension, at the cost of running a forked server.

pricing.notes: Open source; commercial support and enterprise offerings from SKAI Worldwide.

scale.notes: Inherits PostgreSQL streaming replication; no built-in sharding.

strengths: Graph and relational data commit in one ACID transaction inside a single database
SQL, openCypher and ISO GQL clauses can be mixed in one statement
Keeps the PostgreSQL toolchain: pg_dump, replication, row-level security, pgvector
Apache 2.0 and tracking current PostgreSQL releases (18.6 base)
weaknesses: A fork, so it cannot be used on managed Postgres services
Smaller community than Apache AGE or Neo4j
Traversals still execute as relational joins, limiting very deep queries
useCases: Adding graph queries to Postgres-centric systems
Teams experimenting with ISO GQL on familiar infrastructure
